issues.legal_issue: Applying a tenant-protective restriction on transferee-landlords to pending eviction proceedings is a reasonable restriction on property rights and does not violate equality guarantees.
material_facts: A rent-control law limited the grounds on which landlords could recover possession from tenants.

The legislature added a restriction on transferee-landlords seeking eviction, responding to a growing pattern of property transfers followed by eviction litigation aimed at re-letting at higher rents or rebuilding for greater profits.
The amendment expressly applied to suits and appeals already pending when it commenced.
The challenges relied on the effect of that retrospective application on landlords whose proceedings had begun before the amendment.
issues.conclusion: The retrospective application of the restriction to pending proceedings is valid and does not violate Articles 14 or 19(1)(f), read with Article 19(5).
issues.legal_principle: The presumption of constitutionality places the burden on the challenger to establish a clear constitutional violation; courts review the constitutionality, not the wisdom, of the legislature’s chosen classification or remedy. The majority applied Articles 14 and 19(1)(f), read with Article 19(5), and relied on the principles in State of Bombay v. R.M.D. Chamarbaugwala and Shri Ram Krishna Dalmia v. Shri Justice S.R. Tendolkar. It also held that the legislature could reasonably extend the restriction to pending proceedings to address the targeted social harm, notwithstanding individual hardship.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_retroactive_: A party challenged the retrospective application of a tenant-protective restriction as unconstitutional.
predicates.pending_eviction_proceeding: An eviction suit or appeal was pending when the new restriction took effect.
predicates.transferee_landlord: The landlord seeking eviction had acquired the premises by transfer.
predicates.law_targets_widespread_speculative_evict: The legislature enacted the restriction to address a growing pattern of transferee-landlords using eviction proceedings to obtain greater returns from premises.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns applying a tenant-protective restriction to a pending eviction proceeding by a transferee-landlord, and the law addresses widespread speculative evictions, the restriction remains valid retrospectively.

issues.legal_issue: More protective eviction requirements enacted for tenants apply to eviction proceedings that were pending when the amendment commenced.
material_facts: The amendment replaced an earlier eviction ground with more restrictive requirements for rebuilding and for the landlord’s own occupation.
The amendment expressly provided that its changes applied to pending suits and appeals.
The eviction proceedings had originally been brought under the earlier ground, before the landlords could have anticipated the new requirements.
issues.conclusion: The new requirements for eviction apply to pending proceedings, and landlords may be given an opportunity to establish the requirements applicable to their cases, with tenants able to rebut that evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The majority read the express provision covering pending suits and appeals as applying the amended eviction grounds to those proceedings. It treated the more protective requirements as a permissible retrospective change and preferred an interpretation that gives effect to the statute while avoiding unnecessary litigation.

predicates.pending_rent_eviction_case: A suit or appeal seeking eviction under a rent-control law remained pending when the amendment commenced.
predicates.amendment_expressly_covers_pending_cases: The amendment states that its changes apply to suits and appeals already pending.
predicates.amended_eviction_criteria_give_tenants_a: The amendment adds stricter requirements that a landlord must satisfy to recover possession.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction case is pending, the amendment expressly covers pending cases, and the amended criteria give tenants additional protection, those criteria apply in that case.

issues.legal_issue: A pending eviction suit originally pleaded on superseded grounds may proceed on fresh pleadings under the amended grounds, with institution for the new grounds treated as occurring when those pleadings are filed.
material_facts: The transferee-landlords had filed eviction suits under the earlier version of the law, before the amended grounds existed.

The amendment applied to pending suits and appeals and restricted suits based on the amended grounds during a post-transfer waiting period, subject to an exception for certain safety-related cases with permission.
The landlords could not have pleaded the amended requirements when they first filed their suits.
By the time fresh pleadings could be filed in the cases before the Court, the waiting period after the transfers had elapsed.
The Court directed that the tenants be allowed to respond and that the parties be allowed to present additional evidence.
issues.conclusion: The landlords may file fresh pleadings setting out the applicable amended grounds in the pending suit or appeal; the suit is treated as instituted on those grounds when the fresh pleading is filed, subject to the waiting-period requirement or the applicable safety-related permission.
issues.legal_principle: The majority construed “institute” in its natural and grammatical sense as beginning proceedings on the specified grounds. Because the earlier suits were pleaded on grounds that were not the amended grounds, the new restriction on institution did not attach to them until fresh pleadings were filed. The Court preferred a construction that gives effect to the tenant protections while avoiding needless re-litigation, and allowed further pleadings, responsive pleadings, and additional evidence.

rule.if: pending_transferee_landlord_eviction_case and original_pleading_uses_superseded_grounds and landlord_files_fresh_pleading_on_amended_grounds and (post_transfer_wait_elapsed or safety_permission_obtained)

predicates.pending_transferee_landlord_eviction_cas: An eviction suit or appeal by a landlord who acquired the premises by transfer is pending.
predicates.original_pleading_uses_superseded_ground: The landlord’s original pleading relies on grounds that the amendment replaced or altered.
predicates.landlord_files_fresh_pleading_on_amended: The landlord files a new pleading setting out the eviction grounds required by the amended law.
predicates.post_transfer_wait_elapsed: The period that must pass after the landlord acquired the premises has elapsed before the new pleading is filed.
predicates.safety_permission_obtained: The landlord obtained the required permission for an early suit based on a safety-related need for building work.

issues.definition: In a pending eviction case brought by a transferee-landlord on superseded grounds, a fresh pleading on amended grounds counts as institution on those grounds when filed, provided the waiting period has elapsed or the required safety permission has been obtained.
